entries.title: [A0] Set up advisory PR review with thermo-nuclear and unslop
entries.problem: Every core implementation PR needs the same advisory engineering and prose review used in Astroix from the start. Kiero main currently has no application workspace or review workflow, so setup must work before application bootstrap and before the independent corpus and environment PRs.
entries.solution: Install a Kiero-specific version of Astroix AI review: the vendored thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review and unslop skills, local repository rules and accepted glossary, and a standalone GitHub Actions workflow using the Z.AI Coding Plan through Claude Code Action. Review each eligible PR in its code and discussion context, then publish advisory comments. The owner requested this addition after the original charter. Establish this setup before A1, E1 and I1; those three remain independent after A0 closes. The source reference is the verified Astroix commit d4f1bc218261cf6c76984ca2c384df7f7b5bd80e.
acceptance: Preserve the Astroix PR flow: pull_request opened, synchronize, reopened and ready_for_review; skip draft and fork PRs; cancel superseded runs through a per-PR concurrency group; use a 30-minute job timeout. Record the reviewed PR head SHA. Use pull_request, not a privileged pull_request_target job that executes PR code.

Use the repository Actions secret ZAI_API_KEY for https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic, with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and the action anthropic_api_key input. Match the reference configuration: glm-5.3 as reviewer and Opus/Sonnet mapping, glm-5.3-flash as Haiku mapping, max effort and API_TIMEOUT_MS=3000000. Verify the configured route during the actual smoke run and record failures rather than inventing a working model.

Start from anthropics/claude-code-action@62529b7c89dbb8cfaa838f2c87f2f8459b46fe68, the SHA pinned in the reference. Pass github.token explicitly so posting uses github-actions[bot] and does not require installing the Claude GitHub App. Keep contents: read, pull-requests: write, include_fix_links: false and an explicit inspection/comment tool allowlist. Record any necessary action-version change and its reason.

Vendor both skill directories including their LICENSE files, with upstream version/provenance in .agents/skills/README.md. Preserve the imported skill text; put Kiero-specific adaptation in the review prompt and repository instructions. Commit the accepted Kiero CONTEXT.md from the handoff snapshot without changing domain meanings. Create concise Kiero AGENTS.md rules compatible with the execution charter, including rtk, one issue per PR and independent parallel lanes.

The prompt applies thermo-nuclear review to engineering choices and unslop to changed prose and reviewer output, reads Kiero AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md, and inspects the full diff plus relevant surrounding files. Recover prior rounds from PR comments, verify fixes wherever they landed, keep explicitly rejected or overruled findings closed, and avoid repeating deterministic check findings.

Post one advisory summary per PR and edit it across pushes using the reference gh pr comment --edit-last --create-if-none --body-file flow, with inline comments only for high-conviction actionable findings. Publish at the end of the run; a canceled or superseded run must not replace the current review. The reviewer does not edit code, push commits, merge, approve or request changes as a merge gate.

AI review is advisory and is not added to required status checks. Findings do not fail deterministic CI. Authentication, provider or runner failures remain visible as operational failures and cannot be reported as completed reviews. Missing ZAI_API_KEY yields a clear setup diagnosis without printing its value.

The A0 workflow runs in the pre-application repository with no dependency on A1 package.json, lockfile, build, fixtures or CRAP tooling. Use a suitable standalone Node runtime for the pinned action, matching Node 24 in the reference where supported. Omit Astroix-specific npm installs, e2e/fixture, crap:ci, thresholds and legacy product paths. A1 later owns deterministic checks.yml independently.

Treat same-repository PR contributors as trusted for the credential-bearing review job; draft/fork skipping and read/comment limits must remain explicit. Scope the Z.AI secret to the review invocation, keep checkout credentials from becoming persisted write credentials, and keep secret values out of files, prompts, comments and evidence.

After the owner adds ZAI_API_KEY, prove the workflow on a real Kiero PR and a subsequent push before closure. Integrate the setup into main through its own PR. Attach run and comment links, exact commit/configuration, observed outcomes and any remaining setup blocker. File presence or a skipped job is not successful activation.
tests: Validate workflow syntax and pinned action inputs, all referenced skill/instruction paths and licenses in a fresh pre-A1 checkout. Confirm no application install, package script or Astroix-only path is required.

Exercise draft-to-ready, opened/synchronize and reopened handling; verify the current head is reviewed. Test rapid pushes and inspect canceled runs and comment timestamps to ensure old output cannot replace the latest summary.

Use a controlled real PR with a clear engineering defect and slopped prose to verify both skills are applied. Push the fix and verify the same summary comment is updated, corrected findings disappear and new high-conviction findings remain reportable. Verify owner rulings from the thread are respected.

Check draft and fork event conditions without supplying real secrets to an untrusted fork. Check missing-secret behavior in an isolated no-secret validation. Redact all authentication data from logs and evidence.

Inspect live required checks and workflow permissions. Confirm advisory review is not required for merge and cannot write repository code. Document any GitHub Actions permission restriction as a concrete setup blocker.
After integration, record main containing the workflow and the successful run/comment evidence. A1, E1 and I1 must start their PRs from a base that includes this setup.
integration: Producer: standalone .github/workflows/ai-review.yml plus vendored review skills and Kiero instructions. Consumers: every later implementation PR, beginning with A1, E1 and I1.

A1 owns .github/workflows/checks.yml and future application dependency setup. Preserve A0 review files and accepted glossary when importing the handoff documents. This separation avoids an A0/A1 dependency cycle.

The owner supplies ZAI_API_KEY through the repository secret store. Provisioning this secret is separate from OPENROUTER_API_KEY, which remains the application model credential. Verify names and access without reading secret values.

Reference workflow: [Astroix AI review](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/astroix/blob/d4f1bc218261cf6c76984ca2c384df7f7b5bd80e/.github/workflows/ai-review.yml). Reference skills: [thermo-nuclear](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/astroix/blob/d4f1bc218261cf6c76984ca2c384df7f7b5bd80e/.agents/skills/thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review/SKILL.md), [unslop](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/astroix/blob/d4f1bc218261cf6c76984ca2c384df7f7b5bd80e/.agents/skills/unslop/SKILL.md), and [vendoring provenance](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/astroix/blob/d4f1bc218261cf6c76984ca2c384df7f7b5bd80e/.agents/skills/README.md). Local source: /Users/woji/Dev/playground/Astroix. Recheck any later upstream change before adapting it.
nonGoals: Application implementation, Convex/Cloudflare provisioning, OpenRouter calls, deployment or final UX/UI.
Adding AI review to branch protection as a required merge gate, automatic fixes or merges, or importing Astroix product-specific tests and CRAP metrics.
Changing any existing accepted domain decision or editing the Astroix repository.

audit.implemented: Advisory AI PR review workflow and vendored thermo-nuclear/unslop review instructions.
remaining: Closure proves repository integration; retain current successful-run/comment evidence in the map register, not only the historic issue claim.

entries.title: [B1] Implement Google and email-code sign-in with live sessions
entries.problem: Kiero needs real Google and email-code sign-in before any protected company data can be exercised. Identity, session and company membership are separate records: a valid provider token identifies a person but must never grant company access by itself.
entries.solution: Integrate the pinned Convex Auth candidate with Google and Resend-backed Polish one-time email codes. Persist app-owned live-session metadata, activity and revocation state, enforce the accepted 30-day inactivity rule, and resolve every protected request through current session plus membership checks. Keep the codebase and schemas in English and the barebones sign-in states in Polish. Decode provider callbacks and callable inputs with pinned Effect 4 RC schemas and Convex validators; no unchecked cast or `any` may bridge an external boundary.
acceptance: Google and email-code flows create or resume the correct person identity without creating a company membership.
The session registry exposes current device sessions, trusted activity time and explicit revocation state for downstream access checks.
A session expires after 30 days of inactivity and current protected reads reject revoked or expired sessions even when an upstream token remains cryptographically valid.
Sign-in errors, expired codes and resend states have usable Polish UI copy without visual-system work.
Pinned package versions and the exact Convex Auth integration route are recorded with repeatable P02 evidence; candidate status is not described as proven before the checks run.

Own the reusable Resend application-email adapter used by OTP and B3 invitations. Configure real server-side development bindings and prove delivery, expiry, retry identity and safe failure without logging codes or secrets.
tests: Integration-test both providers against their real adapters, including wrong, reused and expired email codes and Google callback failure.
Keep an existing valid token, revoke its app session, and prove a fresh protected query and subscription are denied immediately.
Advance inactivity beyond and just inside 30 days and assert deterministic expiry behavior.
Send malformed callback and session payloads through Effect Schema and Convex validators and assert typed failures.
nonGoals: Account-method linking, invitations, company creation, GM access, production visual design and password authentication.
integration: Produce the identity and live-session resolution operation consumed by B2, B3 and every protected Convex or gateway boundary; register it through A3's typed operation/runtime composition seam rather than exposing auth package tables directly.

audit.implemented: Google and Resend email-code sign-in plus live sessions.
remaining: Real email and Google account flows require configured provider credentials and device evidence.
Runtime reads RESEND_API_KEY while infra/bindings/convex-functions.md names AUTH_RESEND_KEY.

CLOSED and integrated through [PR #78](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/pull/78), merge [`1ea856e57cf4`](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/commit/1ea856e57cf4ded1e77de233036f825c0f7259b2), verified in reviewed main `4aa1cc64b3ecab669c76ffa672832d4c5638ac68`. This is historical implementation completion. Final core qualification is still open.

Google and Resend email-code sign-in plus live sessions.

## Evidence and its limits

- https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/20
- https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/pull/78
- convex/integrations/email/resend.ts
- docs/implementation/proof-ownership.md (P02)

## Remaining qualification or repair work

- Real email and Google account flows require configured provider credentials and device evidence.
- Runtime reads RESEND_API_KEY while infra/bindings/convex-functions.md names AUTH_RESEND_KEY.

Tracked owners: [B5 #134](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/134), [J4 #63](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/63), [J5 #64](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/64). Read each follow-up for its acceptance and native blockers. Keep this historical issue closed; newly discovered defects get an explicit prerequisite.

## Native blockers

[A3 #18](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/18)

Query native `blocked_by` immediately before claiming. All listed blockers must be closed with their required evidence. A closed historical issue supplies integrated code; follow-up repairs and qualifications remain separate.

---

## Original accepted implementation scope

The following records the original issue. Historical status and readiness statements below are superseded by the current inventory above.

Part of [Implementation map: Kiero core MVP and barebones PWA](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/15). Chartered by [Grilling: kryteria gotowości i przekazanie MVP do implementacji](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/13).

**Area:** access. **Proof ownership:** P02.

Read the [execution charter](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/e47f1beb36a864fdb06a50d9ab52f9420cef2178/docs/implementation/execution-charter.md) and [alpha readiness contract](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/e47f1beb36a864fdb06a50d9ab52f9420cef2178/docs/mvp/alpha-readiness.md) before implementation. Relevant decisions: [Grilling: logowanie, zaproszenia i dostęp do firmy](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/4#issuecomment-5574288760), [Grilling: architektura, stack i hosting MVP](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/11#issuecomment-5590547919).

## Problem statement

Kiero needs real Google and email-code sign-in before any protected company data can be exercised. Identity, session and company membership are separate records: a valid provider token identifies a person but must never grant company access by itself.

## Bounded solution

Integrate the pinned Convex Auth candidate with Google and Resend-backed Polish one-time email codes. Persist app-owned live-session metadata, activity and revocation state, enforce the accepted 30-day inactivity rule, and resolve every protected request through current session plus membership checks. Keep the codebase and schemas in English and the barebones sign-in states in Polish. Decode provider callbacks and callable inputs with pinned Effect 4 RC schemas and Convex validators; no unchecked cast or `any` may bridge an external boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Google and email-code flows create or resume the correct person identity without creating a company membership.
- The session registry exposes current device sessions, trusted activity time and explicit revocation state for downstream access checks.
- A session expires after 30 days of inactivity and current protected reads reject revoked or expired sessions even when an upstream token remains cryptographically valid.
- Sign-in errors, expired codes and resend states have usable Polish UI copy without visual-system work.
- Pinned package versions and the exact Convex Auth integration route are recorded with repeatable P02 evidence; candidate status is not described as proven before the checks run.
- Own the reusable Resend application-email adapter used by OTP and B3 invitations. Configure real server-side development bindings and prove delivery, expiry, retry identity and safe failure without logging codes or secrets.

## Focused verification

- Integration-test both providers against their real adapters, including wrong, reused and expired email codes and Google callback failure.
- Keep an existing valid token, revoke its app session, and prove a fresh protected query and subscription are denied immediately.
- Advance inactivity beyond and just inside 30 days and assert deterministic expiry behavior.
- Send malformed callback and session payloads through Effect Schema and Convex validators and assert typed failures.

## Producer and consumer integration

- Produce the identity and live-session resolution operation consumed by B2, B3 and every protected Convex or gateway boundary; register it through A3's typed operation/runtime composition seam rather than exposing auth package tables directly.

## Scope exclusions

- Account-method linking, invitations, company creation, GM access, production visual design and password authentication.

## Parallel-session ownership

Owned paths:

- `convex/access/identity/**`
- `apps/web/src/features/sign-in/**`
- `convex/integrations/email/**`

Use the certified shared interface. Do not edit a parallel sibling's paths or independently rewrite root manifests/lock, generated clients, schema/router/gateway composition or shared deployment state. A missing shared interface becomes a named prerequisite with native blocking. Feature registration and the declared consumer proof are part of this issue; later J joins own the explicit cross-module paths.

## Native blockers

- [[A3] Prove Convex, Effect and durable executor composition](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/18)

GitHub `blocked_by` relations are execution authority. Re-query before claiming; category and issue number do not imply a serial order.

## Session completion

- One claimed issue, one issue-specific worktree branch, one reviewable PR.
- Preserve unrelated changes and stage explicit files. Use ignored environment injection; never print or commit secret values.
- Before integration, reconcile current main and run the focused checks plus required repository checks on the combined result.
- Record exact revision, environment, procedure and observed evidence; keep missing or failed live proofs explicit.
- Close only after integration and required evidence. Then synchronize the canonical checkout safely, remove only this completed worktree, and reconcile newly unblocked work.

entries.title: [B2] Implement verified account linking and session recovery
entries.problem: A boss may sign in through Google or an email code, but matching email text is not proof that two identities belong to one person. Recovery must preserve membership and authorship while preventing a takeover through automatic account merging.
entries.solution: Implement an explicit linking ceremony that starts from a live B1 session and proves control of both methods before attaching them to one account. Serialize concurrent attempts, preserve a canonical account identity, and reject link operations that would merge two established accounts without a supported resolution. Add barebones Polish account controls for adding a method, changing email after reauthentication and listing or revoking sessions. Define the checked manual-recovery command here, but leave its invoker unavailable until B4 supplies explicit GM authority. Recovery records the verification basis, invalidates old sessions and requires fresh method setup while keeping historical actor IDs stable.
acceptance: Both Google-to-email and email-to-Google linking require fresh proof from each method and end at one account, membership history and author identity.
Same-email sign-in without the linking ceremony never merges accounts.
Email change requires recent authentication plus a code sent to the new address.
Session controls revoke one device or all other devices through B1's live-session operation.
Recovery preserves company membership and historic authorship, records the GM actor and verification basis, and revokes every pre-recovery session.
tests: Race two link attempts in opposite directions and prove one canonical result without duplicate identities or memberships.
Attempt linking with one stale proof, one mismatched address and two already-established accounts; assert typed rejection and no partial writes.
Recover an account while an old token and subscription remain open, then prove new protected requests fail.
Verify a failed new-email confirmation leaves the old method and sessions unchanged.
nonGoals: Changing company membership, implementing an automated public recovery desk, building the GM recovery UI, passwords or email-address-based implicit merging.
integration: Consume B1 identity/session operations and register linked-method and recovery commands as A3 typed operations. B4 supplies the only alpha GM invoker for manual recovery; B3 and audit consumers continue to reference the stable account ID rather than provider identities.

audit.implemented: Verified account-linking ceremony and session-recovery behavior.
remaining: Requires real linked-account and recovery exercise under the selected auth configuration.

entries.title: [B4] Implement explicit audited GM access and operations authority
entries.problem: During alpha Wojtek needs global operational access, but a hidden superuser shortcut would corrupt authorship, read metrics and tenant guarantees. GM authority must be explicit, current, auditable and tied to active alpha participation.
entries.solution: Add a separate GM grant and explicit enter/exit mode on top of B3 access resolution. Each GM request states the target company and purpose, records the real GM actor, and checks that both the grant and the company's alpha participation remain active. Build a spare Polish GM panel for inspection and allowed domain commands. GM may inspect sources, runs and company UI, retry failed stages or request linked reanalysis under the app-owned model configuration. It cannot impersonate a boss, edit immutable source content, bypass domain validators, select arbitrary models or perform direct database repair.
acceptance: GM access works without adding an ordinary company membership and is visually unmistakable in the barebones UI.
Every GM read and command produces a protected audit record with GM actor, target company, operation, reason and outcome.
Opening conversations in GM mode does not change boss read states, unread counts or autonomous alpha-use metrics.
Ending company alpha participation removes grant-derived access immediately; time elapsed alone does not end it.
Retries and reanalysis use the same checked domain operations as ordinary processing and preserve the original source plus linked run history.

Provide explicit GM company activation/first-admin invitation, verified manual account recovery through B2, administrator restoration and ending alpha participation. Preserve membership/history while revoking old recovered sessions. This completes the operator control path rather than depending on direct database edits.
tests: Attempt GM access without a grant, after grant revocation and after alpha participation ends; assert denial with no target data leak.
Open and mutate allowed records in GM mode and prove ordinary read and usage counters remain unchanged.
Submit an arbitrary model ID, immutable-source edit and raw database patch through GM endpoints; all must fail validation.
Race grant revocation with a command and require current authority at commit.
nonGoals: A production support-role hierarchy, silent impersonation, unrestricted database consoles or model experimentation.
integration: Extend B3 current-access resolution with an explicit GM branch. Register audit writes and approved retry/reanalysis commands through A3; E3/E4 and operations consumers resolve GM authority again when work commits.

audit.implemented: Explicit, audited GM access grant and enter/exit authority mode.
remaining: GM revocation and real operator behavior require final P02/J5 evidence.

entries.title: [C3] Implement versioned typed extensions and catalog reuse
entries.problem: Firm-specific facts cannot all fit a fixed core, but a free-form JSON or prose bucket would create duplicate meanings and untraceable schema drift. Historical values must remain interpretable after labels or shapes change.
entries.solution: Implement versioned extension definitions as bounded data. Support text, quantity with unit, boolean, enum, financial, temporal, approved entity references, objects and bounded lists. Use stable definition and field IDs, shared product-owned definitions, firm-owned definitions, immutable versions and usage counters derived from persisted values. Before creating a definition, expose catalog search and similarity candidates to the agent, while requiring meaning and type compatibility rather than a name match. Adding an optional firm field creates a new version; incompatible meaning or type requires a new definition or explicit migration.
acceptance: Every extension value validates against the exact stored definition version and keeps C2 revision/provenance history.
Historic values render under their original version after labels, optional fields or newer versions appear.
Firm definitions never change another tenant's catalog; only product code can publish shared definitions.
Usage counts come from committed records and support reuse statistics without model estimates.
Definition payloads remain non-executable and cannot introduce TypeScript keys, functions, queries or unbounded recursive shapes.
tests: Create equivalent names with incompatible units or meanings and prove the catalog does not silently reuse them.
Version millimetres to an incompatible centimetre meaning and require a new definition or explicit migration.
Submit recursive, oversized, executable-looking and cross-tenant schemas through Effect and Convex validators.
Race duplicate-definition proposals and verify one reusable result plus correct atomic usage counts.
nonGoals: Letting AI change the fixed core, executable user schemas, automatic promotion to shared definitions or a rich schema-builder UI.
integration: Consume C2 finding/revision publication. Produce catalog lookup, validate-value and version-registration operations for E6 tools and GM statistics; register bounded schemas through A3 rather than bypassing validators with dynamic casts.

audit.implemented: Versioned typed extension definitions and reusable catalog values.
remaining: Final P06 and UI integration evidence remains open.

entries.title: [C4] Implement tasks, independent checklists and dated events
entries.problem: Tasks, checklist steps and events encode different claims. Treating a date as a task, deriving parent completion from checklist ticks or assuming an elapsed event occurred would create false obligations and false history.
entries.solution: Implement typed task, one-level checklist and event records tied to C1 projects and C2 findings. Tasks use To do, In progress, Waiting, Done and Cancelled; Waiting requires a concrete reason. Events use Planned, Occurred and Cancelled. Separate external executor contacts from coordinator memberships. A task may share a temporal finding with an event only when evidence explicitly links them. Parent completion is an independent sourced command: 3/3 checklist items cannot complete it, and Done with 2/3 is valid. Project closure preserves open administrative work in the company queue.
acceptance: Task, item and event changes create immutable history with actor, time and evidence basis.
Checklist items inherit task coordinator and reminders; an item needing its own owner or date converts to a linked task.
Removing a coordinator membership unassigns open tasks or assigns an explicit successor, while done/cancelled tasks stay closed.
Elapsed planned events remain planned and overdue until explicit occurrence or cancellation evidence arrives.
Closing or cancelling a project changes only obligations clearly covered by the source and keeps unresolved work visible.
tests: Complete every checklist item and assert parent remains open; complete parent with an unchecked item and preserve item state.
Pass a delivery date without an obligation and prove only an event is created; add an explicit receiver obligation and prove a linked task appears.
Revoke the coordinator and verify open assignment, history and downstream registration while external executor contact stays unchanged.
Race a stale AI completion plan with a newer direct correction and require C2 revision checks.
nonGoals: Nested subtasks, team-capacity scheduling, payroll, automatic completion from time passage or polished work-management UI.
integration: Consume C1 stable entities and C2 findings/publication groups. Produce typed task/event/checklist commands and durable change registrations for E6, notifications and Calendar; dependent event/task creation commits atomically when they share one agreement.

Consume MembershipRevoked to move open-task coordination to the explicit successor or unassigned state, preserving completed/cancelled tasks and historic authorship; publish task changes for reminder recalculation.

audit.implemented: Tasks, one-level checklists and dated events attached to projects/findings.
remaining: Reminder, Calendar and final P06/P08 flows need joint qualification.

## Problem statement

Tasks, checklist steps and events encode different claims. Treating a date as a task, deriving parent completion from checklist ticks or assuming an elapsed event occurred would create false obligations and false history.

## Bounded solution

Implement typed task, one-level checklist and event records tied to C1 projects and C2 findings. Tasks use To do, In progress, Waiting, Done and Cancelled; Waiting requires a concrete reason. Events use Planned, Occurred and Cancelled. Separate external executor contacts from coordinator memberships. A task may share a temporal finding with an event only when evidence explicitly links them. Parent completion is an independent sourced command: 3/3 checklist items cannot complete it, and Done with 2/3 is valid. Project closure preserves open administrative work in the company queue.

## Acceptance criteria

- Task, item and event changes create immutable history with actor, time and evidence basis.
- Checklist items inherit task coordinator and reminders; an item needing its own owner or date converts to a linked task.
- Removing a coordinator membership unassigns open tasks or assigns an explicit successor, while done/cancelled tasks stay closed.
- Elapsed planned events remain planned and overdue until explicit occurrence or cancellation evidence arrives.
- Closing or cancelling a project changes only obligations clearly covered by the source and keeps unresolved work visible.

## Focused verification

- Complete every checklist item and assert parent remains open; complete parent with an unchecked item and preserve item state.
- Pass a delivery date without an obligation and prove only an event is created; add an explicit receiver obligation and prove a linked task appears.
- Revoke the coordinator and verify open assignment, history and downstream registration while external executor contact stays unchanged.
- Race a stale AI completion plan with a newer direct correction and require C2 revision checks.

- Consume C1 stable entities and C2 findings/publication groups. Produce typed task/event/checklist commands and durable change registrations for E6, notifications and Calendar; dependent event/task creation commits atomically when they share one agreement.
- Consume MembershipRevoked to move open-task coordination to the explicit successor or unassigned state, preserving completed/cancelled tasks and historic authorship; publish task changes for reminder recalculation.

## Scope exclusions

- Nested subtasks, team-capacity scheduling, payroll, automatic completion from time passage or polished work-management UI.

- `convex/work/**`

entries.title: [D3] Implement authorized retained-media streaming and range reads
entries.problem: Retained photos and alpha audio must be inspectable without public bucket URLs or bearer links that outlive access. Every new byte-range request must honor current session, membership and source rights.
entries.solution: Build authenticated Worker media routes backed by the private EU R2 bucket. For each full or Range request, forward current identity to the B3/D2 authorization operation, resolve the exact retained representation from the source attachment, then stream `R2ObjectBody` without buffering. Support browser audio seeking, image display and download metadata. Disable shared caching that could bypass checks and use representation IDs rather than caller-supplied object keys. Alpha audio stays playable; photo reads target the retained normalized version or the recorded original exception.
acceptance: Full and valid range responses return correct status, content range, length and media type from the authorized representation.
Every new request rechecks live session, membership, company scope, source lifecycle and attachment relationship.
Object keys, missing objects and foreign source IDs do not reveal tenant data or storage layout.
Revocation denies the next range request and any new playback/download request; already delivered bytes are the explicit physical limit.

entries.title: [D5] Normalize photos and preserve readable source representations
entries.problem: Phone photos are often large or awkwardly encoded, yet handwritten amounts, measurements and orientation must remain readable evidence. Deleting received bytes before a verified durable replacement would break provenance and exports.
entries.solution: Implement post-acceptance normalization through the selected Cloudflare Images binding and private R2. Inputs beyond the binding's proved limit must retain the received original or use the scoped media Container after its exact conversion profile passes P05. Record received, normalized archival and thumbnail representations with hashes, dimensions, transform version and status. WebP is only the first candidate; choose settings from real handwriting and dimension proofs. Verify the normalized object is durable and readable before marking it retained. Remove temporary received bytes only when reference, recovery and quality checks pass. Unsupported input, failed conversion or uncertain quality keeps the received original as the inspectable exception.
acceptance: Normalization never changes the D1 logical source and every vision/evidence reference targets an immutable representation version.
Rotation, dimensions, amounts and handwriting remain readable in the retained archival output for accepted fixtures.
The retained original exception is explicit and exported when normalization cannot safely replace it.
Retries cannot overwrite a representation already referenced by a historical extraction or finding.
Decoder/encoder memory, disk, duration and provider input limits are measured through P05 rather than assumed.
tests: Run real received phone formats, EXIF rotation, handwriting, tiny measurements, oversized files and unsupported/corrupt inputs.
Crash after normalized upload but before verification, and after verification but before received-byte cleanup; reconcile without losing all readable copies.
Race two transform versions and prove immutable IDs plus deterministic retained selection.
Force uncertain quality and assert original retention, pending vision status and correct export/media resolution.
nonGoals: Claiming byte-identical camera retention after successful normalization, visual extraction, public image delivery or permanent source deletion.
integration: Consume D2 accepted attachment ledger and I1 scoped Images/R2 executors. Produce immutable retained-representation registration for D3, E4 and exports; processing registration remains owned by the canonical Convex workflow.

audit.implemented: Photo normalization and readable source representations using Images/R2 boundaries.
remaining: Actual Images binding and representative bytes require external qualification.

entries.title: [F1] Implement per-person source read state and notification preferences
entries.problem: A logical source can appear in the company conversation and several project views, but read state belongs to that one source and one person. Treating projections as copies would create inconsistent unread counts, duplicate notification eligibility, and false alpha usage when GM inspects a company. Conversation mute, task-reminder mute, and snooze are separate controls and need separate durable representations.
entries.solution: Implement company-scoped read-state and personal notification-preference operations behind typed A2 contracts. Store one read record per user and logical source, updated only when the user actually sees the source in Kiero or explicitly marks it read. Delivery, dismissal, or notification clicks do not mark it read. Store project conversation mute, company-entry mute, task-reminder mute, preview-content preference, and company-timezone quiet hours as distinct fields. GM reads use the GM actor context but never write boss read state or alpha activity. Provide query functions for unread projections and delivery eligibility; leave rendering to later tickets.
acceptance: Seeing one mixed-project source marks that source read for the boss in every company/project projection and on every device, without affecting another boss.
GM inspection leaves boss read state and ordinary activity counters unchanged.
Conversation mute, company-entry mute, task-reminder mute, snooze, and quiet hours can be changed independently.
Every mutation resolves current company membership server-side and rejects cross-company identifiers.
tests: Integration test two bosses, two projects, one shared source, multiple subscriptions, and GM reads against real Convex mutations/subscriptions.
Failure tests cover revoked membership, forged source/company IDs, concurrent mark-read calls, and a projection that disappears while being viewed.
Contract tests prove notification eligibility consumes the same source/user identity returned by D1.
nonGoals: Web Push delivery, batching, reminder scheduling, final unread UX, and visual styling.
Inferring read state from operating-system notification events.
integration: Consume B3 actor/membership checks and D1 logical source IDs; export typed read/preference queries for F2, F4, H1, H2, I3, and J integration tickets.
Own only convex/attention/read-state/** and convex/attention/preferences/**. Register exported modules through A4/A2 seams in a small integration change; leave shared full composition to J1/J2/J5.

audit.implemented: Per-person source read state and notification preferences.
remaining: Real personal preference behavior needs device/notification qualification.

entries.title: [H3] Expose search, media anchors and source history
entries.problem: Users need to find evidence across authored text, speech transcripts, image OCR, current findings, and history, then inspect the exact retained representation and correction chain. Search results that omit tenant checks, hydrate stale revisions, or point at obsolete media coordinates would undermine the source-backed memory contract.
entries.solution: Implement unstyled Polish search and source-detail routes over E5 retrieval, D3 authorized media access, C2 revisions, and C5 withdrawal/recomputation state. Search text/transcript/OCR with project, author, and date filters; label semantic/full-text coverage and disclose degraded semantic retrieval rather than interpreting no hit as no fact. Hydrate every result against current company access, source state, and index generation. Source detail shows immutable authored content, all retained representations, transcript/OCR segments and time/coordinate anchors, project fragments, findings/provenance, corrections, withdrawals, and dependent recomputation status. Audio playback uses authenticated range streaming; image highlights resolve against the actual retained normalized/original-exception representation. Paginate history rather than loading one growing object.
acceptance: Search finds representative Polish text, transcript, and OCR evidence with filters and opens the authoritative source/revision.
Withdrawn/deleted/revised evidence cannot appear as current through a stale vector result; degraded retrieval is visible.
Media anchors resolve to D3's current retained representation and require live access for every request/range.
History and correction dependencies are inspectable in Polish barebones UI on mobile and desktop.
Expose source withdrawal and reassignment controls through C5, with impact/history and the original source identity/read state preserved. Do not represent withdrawal as permanent deletion.

Recheck current company access for source metadata, transcript/OCR, revisions and history as well as media. Revocation while source detail is open must discard protected subscriptions/views and deny fresh reads.
tests: Real integration fixtures cover text, long-audio segments, normalized-image OCR coordinates, revised finding, withdrawn source, index generation cutover, and company isolation.
Failure tests revoke membership during playback, delete/replace a representation, return a stale vector ID, fail embeddings, and interrupt pagination.
Browser tests verify filters, deep links, range seek, evidence highlight, correction history, and recomputation status.
nonGoals: Final search relevance tuning or visual design, editing sources, public media URLs, or building E5 indexes.
Cross-feature polished navigation beyond stable routes.
integration: Consume A4, E5 retrieval results, D3 streams, C2 revisions, and C5 dependency state; export stable source URLs used by H1, E6 answers, exports, and future UX.
Own search/source-detail feature paths and register narrowly via A4; defer complete composition to J tickets.

remaining: Evidence links target the paged conversation feed, capped at 120 messages, so sufficiently old source details cannot open.

entries.title: [I2] Implement redacted diagnostics, health checks and cost alerts
entries.problem: Convex Free does not provide the promised native platform-log stream. Alpha operations still need redacted application events, Cloudflare diagnostics, independent silence detection, processing/save/recovery alerts, and all-in cost visibility without leaking sources, transcripts, media, prompts, tokens, or credentials.
entries.solution: Implement a typed diagnostic event boundary in Convex/gateway code and Axiom Personal configuration for the accepted retention window. Emit allowed IDs, status, error class, latency, usage, provider route, and cost metadata from A3 workflows and gateway integrations; resolve protected content only through domain access. Treat telemetry delivery as best effort and canonical audit/domain records as authority. Configure three monitor groups: source-save plus failed/stuck processing; backup freshness/health including an external heartbeat that detects total backend silence; and aggregate costs/limits with owner-visible 400 PLN warning and 500 PLN stronger alert. Track Convex/Cloudflare/R2/Containers/Images/AI/email/observability/backup estimates and provider hard caps. Explicitly label native Convex log history unavailable on Free instead of simulating it.
acceptance: Structured diagnostics cover required operations with trace/run IDs and no source body, transcript, media, prompt, token, secret, or raw provider payload.
Three monitor groups produce useful owner notifications for save/processing, health/recovery, and cost/limit conditions.
A missing-heartbeat test detects backend silence independently of application event delivery.
Dashboards state retention and blind spots accurately; application events do not claim full native Convex logging.
tests: Trigger synthetic save failure, stuck processing, stale backup heartbeat, missing application events, and 400/500 PLN threshold crossings in isolated staging.
Snapshot/redaction tests feed adversarial source text, filenames, prompts, auth headers, URLs, and provider errors and assert no sensitive fields reach the sink.
Fault tests drop/duplicate/out-of-order telemetry and prove domain workflows remain correct.
nonGoals: Building a custom logging platform, upgrading to Convex Pro, storing content in logs, or treating telemetry as audit history.
Implementing backup/export/AI business workflows.

entries.title: [I3] Export consistent company snapshots with protected downloads
entries.problem: A company administrator needs a portable, readable export while the company remains active. Reading tables and media at different times would produce an internally inconsistent archive; static bearer downloads could survive admin revocation or permanent source deletion and expose another tenant's data.
entries.solution: Implement an asynchronous export operation anchored to one consistent company snapshot/revision. Assemble a bounded archive in the selected export worker containing a readable escaped HTML index, versioned JSON, source/finding/task/event/extension/history data, and every retained media representation referenced by that snapshot. Export the accepted shared business records, their authorship and history. Personal read/notification settings and Calendar connection/hide/cursor state are account or integration state, not part of the business archive; shared tasks/events remain included. Exclude authentication secrets, platform backups, diagnostics content, provider tokens and other tenants. Store export-source links for invalidation. Downloads use an authenticated gateway check for current company administrator rights on every request, expire 24 hours after completion, support bounded streaming, and become inaccessible immediately if a later permanent source deletion affects the archive.
acceptance: Concurrent company writes do not create mixed-revision JSON, HTML, history, or media; the archive declares its snapshot time/schema version.
HTML and archive paths safely escape hostile user content, and no record/media from another company can enter the result.
Only a current administrator can start or download an export; revocation, expiry, or linked permanent deletion invalidates access immediately.
Completed bytes are cleaned after the 24-hour window or invalidation and status remains auditable.
tests: Run a real export while continuously writing tasks/sources and compare every JSON/HTML/media reference to the declared snapshot.

Adversarial tests cover HTML/script content, path traversal filenames, huge media, missing object, cross-tenant IDs, admin transfer/revocation during assembly/download, range requests, and deletion after completion.
Verify partial archives never become downloadable and retry does not create divergent published snapshots.
nonGoals: Platform backup, public share links, import/restore, final export UX, or exporting authentication/provider secrets.

integration: Consume C3/C4 domain snapshots, D3 retained-media streams and B3 current admin checks; publish export-source links for I4 invalidation and diagnostics to I2.
Own export worker/backend/feature paths. Register a simple Polish status/download screen through A4; defer shared full composition to J.

evidence: The map review and docs/evidence/deletion/README.md record that the real archive worker/download path was unavailable on the I4 lease.

entries.title: [I4] Purge deleted sources and invalidate all derived access
entries.problem: Permanent deletion must remove access immediately and prevent reconstruction through derivatives, search, notifications, Calendar, exports, retries, or later recovery. Database deletion alone is insufficient because media, indexes, remote effects, active streams, and old backup snapshots can outlive the canonical row.
entries.solution: Implement a deletion coordinator that first tombstones the logical source and revokes all application reads atomically, then enumerates provenance/dependency records and durable purge intents for active media, normalized representations, transcripts/OCR, findings/recomputations, vectors/full-text records, notification/push work, Calendar copies, and linked exports. Write a content-free deletion/revocation ledger entry outside application database rollback authority using stable opaque identities and monotonic ordering. Recheck tombstones in every worker before publishing derived output. Invalidate affected I3 archives immediately and purge active/reconstructing content within 24 hours; isolated backup bytes may survive only until reference-aware expiry within 30 days. Record external outcomes as known/unknown and reconcile without making deleted content readable.
acceptance: After the initiating operation commits, source/media/search/export access fails immediately across existing sessions and new requests.
All active and reconstructing derivatives are either verified purged within 24 hours or remain visibly failed/unknown with retry state and alerting.
The external ledger contains no user content yet can prevent resurrection after an old database restore.
Late AI, upload, push, Calendar, export, or index results cannot republish or expose the deleted source.

Expose an administrator-only unstyled impact preview and explicit permanent-delete confirmation, with pending/complete/failed external-cleanup state. This is a real registered feature, distinct from ordinary withdrawal.

Permission checks deny new reads/range requests after the committed tombstone. Bytes already delivered cannot be retracted; active-stream tests report that boundary rather than promise physical erasure of a recipient copy.
tests: End-to-end deletion races active media streaming, image/STT/AI completion, vector indexing, push delivery, Calendar write, export assembly/download, and repeated delete requests.
Fault tests lose acknowledgements and interrupt each purge stage; prove idempotent retry, unknown-outcome reconciliation, 24-hour tracking, and I2 alerts.
Restore an older fixture in quarantine and prove the external ledger suppresses deleted content before access.
nonGoals: Ordinary correction/withdrawal semantics, immediate erasure from isolated backup sets, or legal-policy claims deferred in Q195.
Deleting unrelated user-created Google events.
integration: Consume C5 dependency graph, D3 media authority, E5 search deletion, F3/G3 external intents, and I3 archive links; export ledger/reconciliation contracts to I5/I6 and diagnostics to I2.
Own deletion/purge paths. Producers integrate via typed tombstone checks; global race qualification belongs to J2/J5.

audit.implemented: Closed and integrated, but the implementation does not meet its accepted late-result/deletion invariant.
evidence: Real dev/i4 evidence has 13 PASS and 1 NOT RUN; media read/delete and tombstone denial were exercised.

Static review traces show a queued push retry can reuse a preserved source preview after deletion (convex/operations/deletion/executor.ts, convex/attention/push/operations.ts and convex/attention/push/functions.ts).

Static review traces show existing clarification question/resolution text survives purge and late agent work accepts a tombstoned source (convex/memory/findings/exposition.ts, convex/agent/execute.ts and convex/memory/findings/corrections.ts).
remaining: Invalidate/redact pending delivery payloads and reauthorize each transport against source lifecycle.
Handle existing clarification content with source-aware retention rules and reject late agent writes for non-active sources.
Add prepare-delete-retry and in-flight-agent/deletion interleaving regressions; rerun the I4 live proof plus P09 export row.

entries.title: [I6] Prove quarantine restore with deletion and revocation replay
entries.problem: Backup creation alone does not prove the accepted one-hour recovery point and eight-hour recovery time. Restoring an old snapshot can revive deleted content, revoked sessions, stale memberships, obsolete workflow state, or uncertain Google/push effects unless recovery happens in quarantine and current external constraints are replayed before anything runs. The map review additionally found that I5's checked-in evidence conflicts with a later claimed 13/13 run, and I4 still requires deletion-lifecycle repair. A restore drill cannot turn those unresolved inputs into a pass.
entries.solution: Build a recovery tool and runbook that selects an I10-certified complete backup manifest from the existing `kiero-dev-core` resource topology, restores database plus referenced media into an isolated quarantine target, and keeps users, AI, schedulers, push, email, Calendar, and exports disabled. Apply I4's content-free deletion/revocation ledger in strict order; invalidate restored sessions/method changes as required by B2, purge forbidden content, reconcile retained representations, and classify unknown G3/external outcomes without replaying them blindly. Restore compatible application code, component/auth/workflow versions, configuration schema, and scheduler definitions before validation. Rebuild disposable search projections only after canonical data is safe. Emit a versioned evidence record with snapshot age, elapsed restore time, reconciled counts, unresolved items, and explicit go/no-go; opening access is a separate checked final action.
acceptance: A measured drill restores a complete set with snapshot age at most one hour and reaches validated service readiness within eight hours, or records the target as failed.
No user, worker, AI, or external integration can access/act on quarantine data before ledger replay and validation finish.
Deleted content and revoked access from after the snapshot remain deleted/revoked after restore.
Unknown Calendar/push outcomes are reconciled or safely held, never blindly replayed.

Additive: the selected input is an I10 PASS manifest whose evidence identifies the current backup candidate, actual database snapshot, every referenced retained-media object, manifest-last closure, retention state and scoped credential topology. A unit fixture, incomplete manifest, or ambiguous 13/13 claim is not selectable.

Additive: quarantine isolation must be proved by checked ingress/egress controls: no ordinary user session, service worker, AI route, scheduler, push, email, Calendar, export or public media route may read or act before the final go/no-go. If the existing `kiero-dev-core` refs cannot provide this isolation without creating a new Convex project, record the constraint as OPEN or BLOCKED and keep I6 open pending an owner decision; do not use quota escape as a substitute.

Additive: record post-snapshot deletion of a source, revocation of a membership/session, an outstanding workflow, a missing derived index and an unknown external Calendar/push outcome. Demonstrate the content-free ledger is replayed before search rebuild or external reconciliation and that replay is idempotent after interruption.
Additive: final readiness means validated internal service state only. It neither opens quarantine to users nor activates alpha production.
tests: Perform a real isolated drill with post-snapshot source deletion, session/membership revocation, Google unknown outcome, pending workflow, missing derived index, and scheduler configuration.
Fault injection interrupts restore, ledger replay, media reconciliation, and validation; rerun proves monotonic idempotent progress.
Negative drills use incomplete/corrupt manifests and unavailable dependencies and prove access cannot open.

Measure snapshot age from the complete manifest timestamp and restore elapsed time from restore start through validated readiness. Attach per-stage timestamps, object counts/bytes, ledger counts, revocation counts, workflow/scheduler version checks, unresolved external-effect counts and final `PASS|FAIL|BLOCKED` go/no-go.

Use a deliberate forbidden-media/read and old-session attempt before and after each replay boundary. Prove the attempt is denied before bytes, AI calls, job execution or transport scheduling; retain only redacted artifacts.
Run against the exact revision selected for recovery. Any later I4/I10/runtime change invalidates affected cases and requires rerun; no historic dev lease result is inherited.
nonGoals: Automatic production failover, normal release rollback via database restore, or claiming cross-provider disaster independence.
Changing retention/RPO/RTO policy.
integration: Consume I5 manifests, I4 external ledger, B2 revocation state, G3 reconciliation contracts, and A3 workflow version registry; produce evidence for J5/readiness.
Own recovery tools/evidence only. Any environment opening command must call existing checked authorities rather than patching feature data directly.

Consume I10's complete-backup certificate and D7's real media runtime evidence. Report any restore blocker to its owner rather than changing backup, deletion, identity, Calendar or deployment behavior in this issue. I6 supplies only P10 restore/replay evidence to J5.
resources: Use only refs and deployment capacity under existing `kiero-dev-core`, as required by owner comment #15-5618841487. Do not create a new Convex project to evade quota.
Reserve one exclusive quarantine ref, backup-manifest input, media namespace and recovery operator window. Other jobs must not share its schema, scheduler, media keys or evidence fixture IDs.
Human-only credentials remain in provider/secret stores. Evidence records names, scope and observed behavior, never values.
closure: Keep I6 OPEN until a real I10-complete backup is restored in proved quarantine with RPO <=1 hour and RTO <=8 hours, and every mandatory replay, isolation and fault case passes. Preserve failed drills; a merged recovery-tool PR is insufficient.

audit.implemented: Open; no restore drill is integrated.
evidence: Native GitHub blockers I4/I5 are closed, but both have material qualification/repair gaps described above.

Its acceptance requires an actual isolated quarantine restore, snapshot age <= 1 hour, validated readiness <= 8 hours, post-snapshot deletion/revocation replay and safe handling of uncertain Calendar/push outcomes.
remaining: Select a complete verified P10 snapshot, create an isolated quarantine target and time the drill.
Inject post-snapshot permanent deletion and session/membership revocation; replay the content-free ledger before any user/worker/AI/external access.
Validate database, every retained-media object, auth/component/workflow/scheduler state, and monotonic retry after restore/ledger/media faults.
Reconcile or hold unknown Google/push effects; never blindly replay them.

entries.title: [I7] Implement compatible release, migration and safe PWA update flows
entries.problem: Schema, workflow, gateway, and PWA releases can overlap old tabs, in-flight durable work, recordings, uploads, and local drafts. Replacing all layers atomically is unrealistic; forced reload or database rollback could lose user input or discard newer data. Production also needs an explicit human trigger after synthetic staging.
entries.solution: Implement pinned GitHub Actions checks and release workflow that deploys an isolated synthetic staging environment, records immutable versions/evidence, and exposes an explicit production trigger. Define expand-migrate-contract releases: add backward-compatible schema/API support, run resumable idempotent migrations in bounded batches with progress, release workers/client while retaining executable support for old workflow versions, then remove compatibility only after measured absence. Provide compatible code rollback/forward repair; never automate old database restoration as release rollback. In the PWA, detect a new version, persist/migrate the local draft first, and show a Polish update prompt only at a safe point. Recording, editing, and upload defer reload; unsupported old clients receive a clear update requirement while their recoverable draft remains available. Security/session revocation stays immediate regardless of client age.
acceptance: A schema expansion, resumable migration, mixed old/new clients/workers, and later support removal complete without corrupting canonical data.
Production deployment cannot happen as an implicit consequence of checks/staging and uses environment-scoped secrets.
PWA update never force-reloads during recording/edit/upload and preserves a draft across client schema migration.
Rollback/forward repair does not restore an old database or resurrect revoked access.
tests: Release rehearsal deploys expansion, interrupts/resumes migration, runs old in-flight workflow and old tab, updates the client, verifies compatibility, then removes old support.
Browser/device tests update during recording, text editing, resumable upload, offline draft, draft-schema change, and unsupported-client recovery.
CI tests wrong-environment secrets, failed staging checks, concurrent release attempt, migration retry, and immediate revocation on an old client.
nonGoals: Automatic production promotion, final update-modal design, blue-green perfection, or using backup restore for routine release recovery.
Changing accepted service plans or feature behavior.
integration: Consume A3 workflow version registry, A4 app host, D4 draft/upload states, F3 service worker/push registration, I1 bindings, and I2 release diagnostics; export release/version evidence to J4/J5.
Own release/migration/PWA-update/infra paths. Feature packages expose compatibility adapters; J tickets perform full cross-feature release qualification.

audit.implemented: Closed and integrated for migration/PWA mechanisms, but its release workflow cannot perform the required staged deployment.
evidence: The review executed the workflow guard command and got MODULE_NOT_FOUND: release.yml calls infra/release/verify-release-target.mjs while the committed entry point is verify-target.mjs.
release.yml deployment steps only echo; there is no web, Convex or Worker deployment. GitHub has no configured environments.
The migration rehearsal passed 9/9; it does not validate a workflow executable path or deployment.
remaining: Repair the guard path and add a regression that executes the exact workflow command.
Provision protected staging/alpha environments and implement actual isolated staging deploy of web, Convex and Workers with scoped secrets.
Prove schema expansion, interrupted migration, old tab/worker compatibility, recording/upload during update, Polish update prompt, rollback/forward repair and no old-database restore.

**Area:** operations. **Proof ownership:** P11.

Relevant decisions: [Grilling: architektura, stack i hosting MVP](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/11#issuecomment-5590547919), [Grilling: szybki wpis i rozmowy firmy w mobilnej PWA](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/6#issuecomment-5574570627).

## Problem statement

Schema, workflow, gateway, and PWA releases can overlap old tabs, in-flight durable work, recordings, uploads, and local drafts. Replacing all layers atomically is unrealistic; forced reload or database rollback could lose user input or discard newer data. Production also needs an explicit human trigger after synthetic staging.

## Bounded solution

Implement pinned GitHub Actions checks and release workflow that deploys an isolated synthetic staging environment, records immutable versions/evidence, and exposes an explicit production trigger. Define expand-migrate-contract releases: add backward-compatible schema/API support, run resumable idempotent migrations in bounded batches with progress, release workers/client while retaining executable support for old workflow versions, then remove compatibility only after measured absence. Provide compatible code rollback/forward repair; never automate old database restoration as release rollback. In the PWA, detect a new version, persist/migrate the local draft first, and show a Polish update prompt only at a safe point. Recording, editing, and upload defer reload; unsupported old clients receive a clear update requirement while their recoverable draft remains available. Security/session revocation stays immediate regardless of client age.

## Acceptance criteria

- A schema expansion, resumable migration, mixed old/new clients/workers, and later support removal complete without corrupting canonical data.
- Production deployment cannot happen as an implicit consequence of checks/staging and uses environment-scoped secrets.
- PWA update never force-reloads during recording/edit/upload and preserves a draft across client schema migration.
- Rollback/forward repair does not restore an old database or resurrect revoked access.

## Focused verification

- Release rehearsal deploys expansion, interrupts/resumes migration, runs old in-flight workflow and old tab, updates the client, verifies compatibility, then removes old support.
- Browser/device tests update during recording, text editing, resumable upload, offline draft, draft-schema change, and unsupported-client recovery.
- CI tests wrong-environment secrets, failed staging checks, concurrent release attempt, migration retry, and immediate revocation on an old client.

## Producer and consumer integration

- Consume A3 workflow version registry, A4 app host, D4 draft/upload states, F3 service worker/push registration, I1 bindings, and I2 release diagnostics; export release/version evidence to J4/J5.
- Own release/migration/PWA-update/infra paths. Feature packages expose compatibility adapters; J tickets perform full cross-feature release qualification.

## Scope exclusions

- Automatic production promotion, final update-modal design, blue-green perfection, or using backup restore for routine release recovery.
- Changing accepted service plans or feature behavior.

## Parallel-session ownership

Owned paths:

- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `tools/migrations/**`
- `apps/web/src/pwa/update/**`
- `infra/release/**`

Use the certified shared interface. Do not edit a parallel sibling's paths or independently rewrite root manifests/lock, generated clients, schema/router/gateway composition or shared deployment state. A missing shared interface becomes a named prerequisite with native blocking. Feature registration and the declared consumer proof are part of this issue; later J joins own the explicit cross-module paths.

entries.title: [J3] Qualify AI quality, fallback behavior and processing latency
entries.problem: Working model calls do not establish Polish extraction, memory correctness, fallback behavior or accepted latency. J2's historical dev proof includes provider windows, proof-only media paths, an old stuck-index observation and 16-400 second processing observations. Its repaired real candidate must be demonstrated, not inferred from code or a previous lease. The corpus provides independent expectations but its voice assets remain pending, so a text-only or synthetic transcript substitute would conceal required STT behavior.
entries.solution: Run the independently grounded corpus through the actual J6-reproved integrated candidate, report every modality and stage, then qualify the chosen provider/model/prompt/schema configuration under the accepted readiness thresholds. Every case starts in an isolated tenant state constructed from its versioned fixture; provider implementation cannot read answer keys. Use real generated voice assets, real retained image/audio paths and the selected retrieval/index route. Preserve all raw sensitive output only in protected systems; publish redacted scorecards and failure artifacts.
acceptance: Each of three full runs achieves at least 48/50 case outcomes with zero critical errors of project, amount, date, commitment or source basis. Required clarification is correct; avoidable clarification on clear evidence lowers quality.

Report STT, image extraction, retrieval and final persisted effects separately. Check prohibited mutations, omitted segments, stale corrections, tenant leakage and incomplete-source handling, not just response text.

Prove the application-owned route order, image capability restriction, unsupported schema/tool responses, stalls and provider failures. User UI has no model selector. Record actual routes and metered costs.

Measure ordinary-source 95% within 60 seconds from full durable acceptance; long audio is measured separately without imposing a duration cap. Preserve useful slower routes according to the accepted throughput policy.
Version inputs and independent expectations. Attach all failures/remediation and candidate evidence; no averaging across runs to conceal a failing run or critical case.

Additive: execute all three 50-case runs against the same identified candidate unless a repair is made; a candidate/provider/prompt/schema/corpus change restarts affected complete runs. Each run must contain 14 text, 16 voice, 12 image and 8 mixed cases with actual assets and clean per-case tenants.

Additive: each case and each run has status PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT RUN. A provider outage is classified separately from application behavior but leaves a mandatory case unqualified; it cannot be averaged away or auto-closed.

Additive: use J6's re-proved retrieval/deletion/provenance/reassignment candidate. Confirm source withdrawal/deletion, current-revision hydration and no stale correction change final memory; a plausible chat response does not pass if persisted state or provenance fails.
tests: Three actual end-to-end corpus executions and separate component diagnostics for failures.
Forced fallback/error/timeout and missing-segment scenarios on the application integration.
Retrieval deletion/revision/cutover, similar aliases, relative dates, unknown tax and approximate/agreed money.

Generate and hash voice assets from the declared fixture content before the first run; reject missing or mismatched assets. Reset tenant, source, model session, queue and index state before every case and verify isolation after teardown.

Collect durable-acceptance to terminal-memory latency for every ordinary text, one-image and <=2-minute audio source. Publish p50/p95/count/outliers; report longer audio separately and never discard it to improve the ordinary cohort.

For every failure, retain the stage trace: acceptance, extraction/STT, image, retrieval, tool call, plan/commit and persisted verification. Reproduce provider fallback/stall using sanctioned fault injection, never altered live credentials.
nonGoals: No fabricated benchmark from provider catalog speeds or substitution for four-week live-alpha metrics.

## Problem and observed evidence

Working model calls do not establish Polish extraction, memory correctness, fallback behavior or accepted latency. J2's historical dev proof includes provider windows, proof-only media paths, an old stuck-index observation and 16-400 second processing observations. Its repaired real candidate must be demonstrated, not inferred from code or a previous lease. The corpus provides independent expectations but its voice assets remain pending, so a text-only or synthetic transcript substitute would conceal required STT behavior.

## Bounded solution

Run the independently grounded corpus through the actual J6-reproved integrated candidate, report every modality and stage, then qualify the chosen provider/model/prompt/schema configuration under the accepted readiness thresholds. Every case starts in an isolated tenant state constructed from its versioned fixture; provider implementation cannot read answer keys. Use real generated voice assets, real retained image/audio paths and the selected retrieval/index route. Preserve all raw sensitive output only in protected systems; publish redacted scorecards and failure artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of three full runs achieves at least 48/50 case outcomes with zero critical errors of project, amount, date, commitment or source basis. Required clarification is correct; avoidable clarification on clear evidence lowers quality.
- [ ] Report STT, image extraction, retrieval and final persisted effects separately. Check prohibited mutations, omitted segments, stale corrections, tenant leakage and incomplete-source handling, not just response text.
- [ ] Prove the application-owned route order, image capability restriction, unsupported schema/tool responses, stalls and provider failures. User UI has no model selector. Record actual routes and metered costs.
- [ ] Measure ordinary-source 95% within 60 seconds from full durable acceptance; long audio is measured separately without imposing a duration cap. Preserve useful slower routes according to the accepted throughput policy.
- [ ] Version inputs and independent expectations. Attach all failures/remediation and candidate evidence; no averaging across runs to conceal a failing run or critical case.
- [ ] Additive: execute all three 50-case runs against the same identified candidate unless a repair is made; a candidate/provider/prompt/schema/corpus change restarts affected complete runs. Each run must contain 14 text, 16 voice, 12 image and 8 mixed cases with actual assets and clean per-case tenants.
- [ ] Additive: each case and each run has status PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT RUN. A provider outage is classified separately from application behavior but leaves a mandatory case unqualified; it cannot be averaged away or auto-closed.
- [ ] Additive: use J6's re-proved retrieval/deletion/provenance/reassignment candidate. Confirm source withdrawal/deletion, current-revision hydration and no stale correction change final memory; a plausible chat response does not pass if persisted state or provenance fails.

- Three actual end-to-end corpus executions and separate component diagnostics for failures.
- Forced fallback/error/timeout and missing-segment scenarios on the application integration.
- Retrieval deletion/revision/cutover, similar aliases, relative dates, unknown tax and approximate/agreed money.
- Generate and hash voice assets from the declared fixture content before the first run; reject missing or mismatched assets. Reset tenant, source, model session, queue and index state before every case and verify isolation after teardown.
- Collect durable-acceptance to terminal-memory latency for every ordinary text, one-image and <=2-minute audio source. Publish p50/p95/count/outliers; report longer audio separately and never discard it to improve the ordinary cohort.

- docs/evidence/ai/run-2.json
- docs/evidence/ai/run-3.json

Up to two non-critical corpus outcome failures per run remain visible under the accepted threshold. A partial run, provider outage or missing voice asset cannot count as a complete run.

Store credentials only in server-side secret stores; record names and presence, never values.

entries.title: [R2] Purge clarification content and reject late source-derived writes
entries.problem:
I4 deletes fragments but not clarifications. convex/memory/findings/exposition.ts:233-243 still returns question and resolutionNote after their evidence disappears, so deleted text can remain visible. convex/agent/execute.ts:69 and 169 accept a retained tombstone because they check existence only. convex/memory/findings/corrections.ts:153-165 checks fragment company ownership but not active lifecycle. Work started before deletion can therefore publish afterward.

The repair needs one active-source rule across creation, resolution, context, final commit and purge. It must remove deleted content while preserving references to independent active evidence.
entries.solution:
Before deleting fragments, I4 finds clarifications linked by conflicting evidence and R1 resolution evidence. It removes associations to the deleted source, replaces possibly derived question or resolution text with fixed Polish redaction copy, records purge metadata, and removes redacted open rows from actionable Memory and Co teraz reads. Keep timestamps, actor and surviving active references. Never summarize deleted text.

Use the accepted source lifecycle, not row existence, in raise, resolve, agent entry, context loading and the final mutation check. A tombstone between model work and commit returns a typed refusal and publishes no event. Purge remains idempotent across each stage and does not delete unrelated findings supported elsewhere.
acceptance: After deletion, no original question, note or deleted reference appears in reads, agent context, search or export.
Redacted open cases are not actionable or shown in Co teraz.
Independent active references and unrelated findings remain.
A late raise or resolve refuses with no event or row.
A tombstone never counts as active.
Each purge stage retries without duplicate events or restored content.

Every affected read refuses or redacts immediately after the source tombstone, before asynchronous purge finishes. Persist only content-free audit metadata for removed text. Process existing rows in bounded idempotent batches and test interruption before each batch.

I4 matrix for open/resolved, conflict/resolution evidence and surviving independent sources.
Barrier race: pause E6, tombstone, resume, assert refusal and no event.
Crash/retry tests around cleanup and fragment deletion.
Cross-company malformed-reference test.
Pause the deletion executor immediately after tombstone and query Memory, Co teraz, agent context and source-backed reads before any physical cleanup; deleted canaries must already be absent.

I6 replays tombstone and redaction state.
I3 and H1/H2 consume sanitized rows.

entries.title: [R4] Reject stale complete source project reassignment
entries.problem:
sources.reassignSource currently accepts only sourceId and a complete replacement projectIds set at packages/contracts/src/modules/sources.ts:81-90. The UI snapshots currentProjectIds once into local state at apps/web/src/features/source-detail/reassign.ts:30-42 and submits only its desired set at lines 58-70. The server reads current links at convex/sources/reassign/reassignment.ts:223-234, then replaces them at lines 243-264 without checking what the editor originally saw.

Race: A and B both open a source assigned to P1. A submits P2. B's stale form submits P1 and P3. The transaction serializes correctly but silently removes A's P2 because B supplied a complete set with no precondition. The later scope reassessment then treats B's stale replacement as intended authority.
entries.solution:
Add an explicit observed-placement precondition to the certified command. The simplest bounded contract is expectedProjectIds, a normalized complete set captured with the read that populated the form. In the reassignment transaction, compare it with the current set before any write, event or recomputation job. Set comparison must ignore ordering and duplicates while preserving tenant validation. A mismatch returns a typed source_placement_stale conflict and the authoritative current set or causes the UI to refetch it through the existing detail read.

After a stale refusal, show clear Polish copy such as "Przypisanie źródła zmieniło się. Odświeżyliśmy aktualny wybór. Sprawdź go i zapisz ponownie." Replace local selected state with current server data. Never merge the stale and current sets automatically because the command declares a complete replacement. Keep the accepted path atomic with its sourceReassigned event and memory recomputation job.
acceptance: The command carries the exact complete project set observed by the editor and refuses if it differs from the current committed set.
Two independently loaded forms reproduce the race: A succeeds, B receives source_placement_stale, and P2 remains assigned.
After B reloads the authoritative set and deliberately submits P1 plus P3, that new command succeeds and has one event and one recomputation identity.
Ordering and duplicate input cannot create a false stale conflict or duplicate link.
Cross-tenant and unknown project checks still occur before writes and do not expose foreign placement.
The UI resets to authoritative placement after a stale refusal and does not display the success notice.
A pre-repair client that omits the observed placement precondition receives a typed reload/upgrade refusal. An optional or defaulted precondition must never bypass concurrency protection.
