Contract tests for required or versioned precondition shape, duplicate normalization and malformed IDs.
Mutation tests for stale mismatch, no-op current replacement, cross-tenant input and one atomic accepted change.
Surface test for Polish stale copy, selection reload and explicit second submit.
Regression through E7 recomputation proof confirming no job or event on stale refusal.
integration: E7 remains owner of complete replacement and recomputation semantics.
Source detail read must return the placement token or complete set from the same snapshot as currentProjectIds.
R5 may later replace source links but does not alter this command.
J5 must include the concurrent-boss stale edit scenario in final core qualification.

entries.title: [R7] Stabilize Calendar protocol timeout tests without hiding failures
entries.problem:
tests/g3/protocol.test.ts defines SHORT_TIMEOUT_MS as 150 at line 53 and passes it through base at line 115 for every protocol call. The same small deadline covers ordinary local HTTP success tests and deliberate timeout tests, which set fake delay to ten times that value at lines 148-154, 220-224 and 321-328. Under machine load, an ordinary first request missed 150 ms in the map review. The focused rerun passed 20/20 and the complete rerun passed, so the observed failure is a test timing race rather than evidence of a production Calendar defect.

The repair must make the local success path tolerant of CI scheduling while retaining a short, deterministic way to prove timeout classification and no blind retry. Increasing every timeout blindly would slow negative tests and can mask an AbortController regression.
entries.solution:
Separate the normal local-server budget from the deliberate timeout budget. Give success and status cases room for CI startup. Timeout cases pass a small explicit deadline and delay the fake response beyond it. A request-received barrier should distinguish timeout-after-request from connection startup. Keep request counts and outcomes.

Do not change EVENTS_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS or add retries unless an independent red test proves a product defect. Timeout remains unknown with cause timeout and one request. A 5xx remains unknown without that cause. Use fake timers only if they reliably drive fetch and AbortController.
acceptance: Normal local HTTP success and status cases use a budget distinct from deliberate timeout cases.
The timeout create, list and observe cases still pass cause timeout explicitly and each records exactly one request.
The 5xx case remains unknown without timeout, and calendar-scoped 401, 403 and 404 mappings are unchanged.
No production timeout constant, retry policy or Calendar protocol code changes in this PR.
Repeated focused runs under ordinary local load complete without the prior first-request flake and without materially lengthening the suite.
A deliberately broken abort classification makes at least one focused test fail.
tests: Prove the smallest failure by running the current focused file repeatedly or with controlled local server startup delay and capture the ordinary success miss without changing product code.
Refactor the harness into NORMAL_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MS and DELIBERATE_TIMEOUT_MS or equivalent explicit per-call controls.
Run npx vitest run tests/g3/protocol.test.ts, then a bounded repeat of that focused file.
Mutation check or temporary local edit showing timeout classification assertion fails when abort is mapped as generic unknown, reverted before handoff.
Run the remaining focused tests/g3 files once to catch harness leakage.
integration: G3 protocol semantics remain the source of truth.
J4 still owns real Google account and long-running Calendar qualification. R7 is local test reliability only.
M0 records the original one-off failure, focused repeat and the new stable focused evidence without rewriting history.
If the reproduction cannot force the flake deterministically, the PR must state that and rely on the controlled startup-delay red proof rather than claim repeated live failure.
nonGoals: Changing production HTTP deadlines
Adding Calendar retries
Real Google API qualification
Broad test-runner tuning
Masking protocol errors with loose assertions or skipped tests

Timeout outcome and one-request trace for create, list and observe

entries.title: [I8] Prepare an isolated qualification environment and prove an actual staging release
entries.problem: The reviewed main has no configured GitHub environments, no Release run, placeholder environment descriptors, and provider binding gaps. The email inventory names AUTH_RESEND_KEY while runtime reads RESEND_API_KEY. Older staging docs prescribe a new Convex project, but the later owner checkpoint requires proof refs under kiero-dev-core and forbids creating projects to escape limits. A green local build cannot supply a representative qualification target.
entries.solution: Establish one named synthetic qualification candidate using R6 executable release tooling and explicit environment-scoped configuration. First reconcile deployment topology with the later owner resource instruction. Prefer an isolated authorized deployment under the existing project; demonstrate equivalent data, credential, scheduler and storage separation. If that cannot satisfy the accepted contract, record the exact decision needed before mutation. Create only authorized resources on accepted plans, install named runtime bindings securely, configure actual GitHub staging/alpha-production protection, and execute one real staging release with post-deploy checks.
acceptance: Publish a resource/binding matrix for web, Convex, gateway, media/export/backup executors, R2, OpenRouter, Google OAuth, email, push VAPID and telemetry. Record each name, consumer, scope, permissions, injection method, presence and observed behavior; never values. Reconcile runtime names including RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM, AUTH_GOOGLE_ID/SECRET and separate media/backup credentials.

Verify actual accounts, quotas, deployment slots and permitted topology before creation. Reuse reserved refs under the existing Convex project; never create projects/accounts or upgrade plans as a quota workaround. Inventory stale resources with owners and evidence before requesting any destructive cleanup.

Synthetic staging must remain isolated from other workers and real company data. Pin deployment IDs, worker/bucket names, OAuth redirect URIs, web origin, environment labels and least-privilege scopes in sanitized evidence. Fixture/probe authorization cannot be enabled on the qualification user path.

Execute R6 workflow against the selected revision. Prove web assets, Convex schema/functions, gateway and required workers match the recorded candidate and health/binding checks. A missing dependency or wrong target returns an explicit blocked/failed outcome, not a successful release.

Create and inspect actual GitHub environment protection, including an explicit production approval requirement. Configuration of production protection does not authorize production deployment. Demonstrate rejection of wrong-environment bindings without touching another environment.

Publish a secure operator procedure for any human-only credential or account action, with destination, exact variable name, successful-check command and responsible actor. Close only when the staging configuration and real release required by downstream tasks work; keep unresolved requirements open.
tests: Run wrong-target, missing-binding, revoked-credential and partial-deployment probes using an isolated target and sanctioned fixtures. Demonstrate safe retry and explicit release outcome.
Smoke test ordinary authenticated access and real service connectivity without proof bypasses. Full identity behavior belongs to B5; full media/backup/export behavior belongs to D7/I10/I9.
Reproduce setup from the committed instructions on a clean checkout; inspect client assets/logs for accidental secret exposure.
integration: Consumes R6 release commands, I1 environment contracts and implemented service adapters. Produces the environment lease and versioned target manifest consumed by B5, D7, I11 and later proof lanes.

Every required case records status `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED` or `NOT RUN`, exact candidate, environment/device, independently expected result, observed result and a repeatable command/procedure. Keep raw failures and provider/configuration versions. Real service or physical-device evidence assigned here cannot be replaced by fixtures. Store credentials only in server-side secret stores; record names and presence, never values.

## Outside this issue

- AI corpus qualification by smoke tests, physical-device certification by emulation, final UI styling or waiving degraded/blocked positive paths.

## Proof ownership

P01, P02, P03, P05, P06, P07, P08. Full-core closure remains [J5 #64](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/64). This task does not approve final design, production activation or four-week live-alpha outcomes.

entries.body:
Part of [Implementation map #15](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/15).

## Assignment

The owner requested a complete reconciliation of every implementation issue after the 2026-09-12 review of main `4aa1cc64b3ecab669c76ffa672832d4c5638ac68`. This task owns the map administration and the matching documentation PR. Application repairs are separate issues; this task does not implement them or activate production.

## Deliverables

- Inventory every original implementation child and the later G5/E7 additions, with merged PR/revision, implemented behavior, actual evidence, limitations and responsible follow-up issues.
- Preserve historical accepted work. Add explicit repair and operational proof issues for review findings and unmet required proofs; update existing I6/J3/J4/J5 scopes and native blockers so incomplete prerequisites cannot be skipped.
- Make every remaining issue executable: exact problem and evidence, bounded solution, acceptance cases, failure/race tests, producer/consumer contracts, owned paths, resource leases, prerequisites, exclusions, evidence outputs and closure conditions.
- Publish an acyclic native GitHub dependency graph and synchronize issue bodies, local manifest, graph, proof ownership, UX coverage and coordinator instructions.
- Audit both the local graph and live GitHub after mutation. Every required repair/setup/proof must reach J5; current readiness must use native blockers, integrated code and proof rather than closed issue counts.

## Acceptance

1. Every original and added implementation issue is inventoried; no accepted core feature or required P01-P12 case loses an owner.
2. All review findings have a concrete repair owner and affected qualification blockers. New issues neither duplicate existing open work nor hide implementation in the final audit.
3. Parallel ready lanes have disjoint implementation ownership or an explicit ordering/lease rule. Shared contract/schema/generated/client/release changes are coordinated.
4. Physical devices, real accounts, provider configuration and elapsed Calendar observation have explicit owners, prerequisites and completion evidence. Required evidence stays open when externally blocked.
5. Read-only local and remote audits confirm exact child membership, issue state/body/dependency agreement, acyclicity, reachable final qualification and expected frontier.
6. One issue-specific documentation branch and PR is integrated with appropriate checks and review; report exactly what changed and what remains for implementation.

## Owned paths

`docs/implementation/**`, `docs/evidence/map-review/**`, relevant documentation index links. GitHub administration of #15 and its implementation issues is explicitly included in this owner assignment.

## Exclusions

Application fixes, infrastructure deployment, secret entry, product-scope changes, production activation and claims of completed core qualification or alpha outcomes.

<!-- kiero-core:M0 -->

## Documentation ownership clarification

This administrative PR owns docs/implementation/**, docs/evidence/map-review/**, the stale status introduction in docs/mvp/architecture-proof-matrix.md and the stale deterministic-check statement in docs/operations/pr-review.md. Accepted proof requirements remain unchanged.

R1, R4, R6 and R7 are the expected first ready tasks after M0. Always query native blockers and current claims before dispatch. Follow R1 → R2 → R3 for provenance/deletion/push safety; R6 → I8 enables actual service qualification. J6 establishes the repaired real candidate for J3/J4. J5 remains blocked until the complete operational, recovery, AI and device evidence is available.

## Evidence and closure

- A closed historical issue means its implementation was integrated. It does not supply a final qualification result for a later candidate.
- Every required case records PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT RUN, exact revision/configuration, independent expected outcome, observed result and a repeatable procedure. Missing mandatory proof keeps its issue open even if a code PR merges.
- J3 requires three complete 50-case runs, each at least 48/50 with zero critical errors, and ordinary-source p95 <=60 seconds. Preserve all non-critical failures; do not average failing runs away.
- J4 requires actual tester phones plus physical iPhone/Android coverage, browser/PWA modes, desktop Chrome/Edge/Safari, two real Google accounts and more than seven real elapsed days. Actual push and release-during-recording/upload are required.
- I6 requires a real complete I10 backup restored in quarantine, post-snapshot deletion/revocation replay before access, RPO <=1 hour and RTO <=8 hours. I9 owns actual export bytes/download/invalidation. I11 owns actual alert transport; J5 joins measured all-in costs.
- J5 traces all accepted core functions and all 61 UX inventory rows to current operations, reachable barebones controls or operator procedures, owners and P01-P12 evidence. New defects become bounded prerequisites with native blockers before affected qualification continues.

## Resources and owner constraints

The [later Convex owner instruction](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/15#issuecomment-5618841487) requires refs under existing `kiero-dev-core` and forbids creating projects to escape quota. I8 must prove isolated staging and I6 isolated quarantine within that constraint. If impossible, keep the owning issue OPEN/BLOCKED and identify the exact owner decision before mutation. Do not assume the older new-project descriptors are authorized.

Credentials, physical devices, two Google accounts, approved alert destinations, service capacity and elapsed time are task prerequisites. Record resource ownership and resumption triggers. Worktrees do not isolate shared cloud deployments. Serialize schema/configuration writers and final integrations; reserve separate fixtures/accounts for parallel proof lanes. Keep credentials in server-side stores and record names, presence and observed behavior only.

## Start and authoritative records

Read the [current implementation package](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/README.md), [coordinator prompt](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/coordinator-start-prompt.md), [complete inventory](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/inventory.md), [dependency graph](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/dependency-graph.md), [full issue manifest](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/issues.json) and [proof ownership](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/proof-ownership.md). Run `rtk proxy node docs/implementation/audit-map.mjs --remote` before dispatch.

One issue, one issue-specific codex/ worktree branch and one PR per implementation assignment. The coordinator may span the map, owns Git lifecycle, fills independent ready lanes and records checkpoints. Scope and accepted meaning remain in [the charter](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/execution-charter.md), [planning map #1](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/1), [readiness #13](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/issues/13), [proof cases](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/mvp/architecture-proof-matrix.md), [UX coverage](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/implementation/ux-coverage.md) and CONTEXT.md.

The [2026-09-12 review](https://github.com/wojtekpiskorz/kiero/blob/main/docs/evidence/map-review/2026-09-12.md) records the baseline defects and evidence limits. M0 #125 reconciles this tracker and documentation; it does not fix application code.
